title: The E-commerce SEO Checklist: 27 Things to Fix Before You Buy More Ads
metaTitle: E-commerce SEO Checklist: 27 Fixes Before More Ads
metaDescription: A 27-point e-commerce SEO checklist covering on-page, technical, content and off-page fixes: the process behind 16x organic traffic growth for one retailer.
excerpt: Before you raise ad budgets again, run this 27-point audit. It is the same on-page, technical, content and off-page process that took one retailer to 16x organic traffic, and every item is something you can check this week.

faqs.q: What should I fix first for e-commerce SEO?
faqs.a: Technical blockers first: crawl the site, fix broken links and redirect chains, resolve indexing errors and Core Web Vitals on your templates. Nothing else matters if Google cannot crawl and render the store properly. Then optimize titles, descriptions and copy on your top 50 revenue pages before investing in new content or link building.

faqs.q: How long does e-commerce SEO take to show results?
faqs.a: Technical and on-page fixes can move rankings within weeks, while content and authority building compound over months. As reference points from anonymized client work: a new services business grew organic traffic 250% in three months, and a UAE fragrance retailer reached 16x organic traffic growth over a sustained campaign.

faqs.q: Do category pages or blog posts matter more for store SEO?
faqs.a: Category pages are the highest-value SEO asset on most stores because they target commercial 'buy' keywords with real volume, and most merchants leave them as bare product grids. Blog content matters for capturing comparison and question searches earlier in the funnel, but optimize categories first.

faqs.q: Are backlinks still important for e-commerce SEO in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. If competitors who outrank you have several times your referring domains, on-page work alone will not close the gap. Links earned through digital PR, linkable assets and product placements remain a primary authority signal: one perfume store's growth campaign included 3,000+ backlinks built over time. Cheap purchased links, by contrast, do nothing at best.

body:
Every dollar of paid traffic you buy lands on a store that either compounds it or wastes it. When organic is broken, you are renting every single visitor forever; when it works, it becomes the cheapest revenue channel you own. We have watched this play out repeatedly: a UAE fragrance retailer we work with grew organic traffic 16x with disciplined SEO, and a brand-new services business grew organic traffic 250% in three months, in both cases by fixing fundamentals before spending more on ads.

This is the checklist we run on every new e-commerce account. Twenty-seven items, four areas. None of them require genius; all of them require actually being done.

## On-Page: Pages That Deserve to Rank

1. Rewrite title tags on your top 50 pages. Lead with the keyword buyers actually search, keep it under 60 characters, and make every title unique. Templated titles like 'Product Name | Store' waste the single strongest on-page signal.

2. Write meta descriptions that sell the click. Under 160 characters, include the offer or differentiator (free shipping, ships today, 2-year warranty). Descriptions do not rank you, but they move click-through rate, which does.

3. Use one H1 per page, matched to intent. The H1 should name the product or category the way customers phrase it: 'Men's Leather Wallets,' not 'Our Collection.'

4. Replace manufacturer product descriptions. Copied descriptions put you in a duplicate-content pool with every other stockist. Rewrite your top sellers first: 150-300 original words covering materials, fit, use cases and objections.

5. Build out category page copy. Categories are your highest-potential pages because they target commercial keywords with real volume. Add 200-400 words of genuinely useful buying guidance (above or below the grid) plus internal links to subcategories.

6. Add descriptive alt text to product images. Describe the product ('black leather bifold wallet, open view'), not the file name. This feeds image search, which quietly drives real e-commerce traffic.

7. Fix internal linking from strength to money. Your homepage and top blog posts carry the most authority: make sure they link to priority categories with descriptive anchor text, not 'click here.'

8. Mark up products with structured data. Product, Offer, AggregateRating and Review schema earn price and star-rich results. Validate with Google's Rich Results Test; a schema error is a free upgrade you are declining.

9. De-duplicate near-identical pages. Size and color variants, filtered URLs and search pages should canonicalize to one primary version. Decide which page you want to rank and point everything else at it.

## Technical: Let Google In, Keep Speed Up

10. Crawl your own site. Run Screaming Frog or a similar crawler and fix what it finds: broken links, redirect chains, missing titles, orphan pages. Most stores have never once been crawled by their owners.

11. Fix Core Web Vitals on templates, not pages. Fixing your product-page template fixes thousands of URLs at once. Prioritize Largest Contentful Paint: compress hero images, serve modern formats, and cut render-blocking scripts.

12. Audit your app and script stack. Every marketing pixel and widget you have added since launch is still loading. Remove what you no longer use; defer what can wait. This is often the single biggest speed win on Shopify stores.

13. Confirm mobile rendering matches desktop. Google indexes the mobile version. If your mobile template hides description copy or internal links, so does your ranking profile.

14. Resolve out-of-stock and discontinued pages deliberately. Temporarily out of stock: keep the page live with a restock signal. Discontinued: 301 to the closest replacement or category, never to the homepage, and never leave a soft 404 farm.

15. Clean up faceted navigation. Filter combinations can generate millions of crawlable junk URLs that drain crawl budget. Canonicalize or noindex parameter pages and keep only genuinely searched combinations indexable.

16. Submit clean XML sitemaps. Sitemaps should contain only canonical, indexable, 200-status URLs. Check Search Console's page indexing report monthly: 'Crawled, currently not indexed' at scale is a quality signal, not bad luck.

17. Verify your redirects from past migrations. If you have ever replatformed, sample old URLs from your analytics history and confirm they still 301 to the right places. Decayed redirect maps silently bleed authority.

18. Use HTTPS everywhere with no mixed content. A single insecure resource can trigger browser warnings that kill both trust and conversion.

## Content: Own the Questions Before the Purchase

19. Map keywords to the full funnel. Rank category pages for 'buy' terms, product pages for model-specific terms, and articles for the comparison and question searches that precede purchase. A store without content competes for only a third of its market's searches.

20. Build comparison and best-of guides. 'X vs Y' and 'best [category] for [use case]' pages capture buyers at the decision point. Be honest in them: credible comparisons convert and earn links; propaganda does neither.

21. Answer real pre-purchase questions. Mine your support inbox and product Q&As for what buyers actually ask, then answer each properly on the relevant page or in a dedicated article. This is also where AI-driven search increasingly pulls its answers from.

22. Refresh instead of only publishing. Update your top existing pages (new year, new products, current prices) before writing new ones. A refreshed page with existing authority usually outranks a new one for months.

23. Kill thin and dead content. Pages with no traffic, no links and no conversions in twelve months should be improved, consolidated or removed. Pruning dead weight measurably lifted quality signals on multiple stores we manage.

## Off-Page: Authority You Cannot Fake

24. Benchmark your link gap. Compare your referring domains against the three competitors who outrank you. If they have five times your links, on-page tweaks will not close the gap: this tells you where the ceiling is.

25. Build links with digital PR and genuinely linkable assets. Data pieces, expert commentary, original guides and supplier or partner relationships earn links that survive algorithm updates. Volume matters when quality is held: we built 3,000+ backlinks for one perfume store as part of the campaign behind its organic growth. What does not work: buying $5 links from farms, at best they do nothing.

26. Get product mentions in gift guides and roundups. Journalists and bloggers compile 'best of' lists year-round, not just in Q4. A steady outreach cadence with samples and a good story wins placements that convert directly and build authority.

27. Treat reviews as an off-page asset. Reviews on Google Business Profile, Trustpilot and marketplace listings shape both rankings and the click decisions around them. Systematize the ask post-delivery; do not leave it to chance.

## Run It in This Order

If you cannot do everything at once, sequence it: technical blockers first (items 10-18), because nothing else matters if Google cannot crawl and render you properly; then on-page on your top 50 money pages (1-9); then content (19-23) as the compounding engine; then off-page (24-27) as the sustained campaign it has to be. Re-run the full checklist quarterly: stores drift, apps accumulate, and redirects decay.

None of this argues against paid ads; we run plenty of them. It argues against buying traffic to a store that leaks it. Fix these 27 items and every channel (paid included) converts better on the same spend. If you would rather have it done than read about it, this checklist is the intake audit for our /marketing/seo/ engagements.
